title_short: Christie Modlin · AYH · Our Women and Children Are Precious
headline: A NIWRC board member answers the three Are You Happy questions: she is happy to work with a great group of women, the sisterhood is why, and her one message is that women and children are precious and deserve to be safe and loved.
story: This is the first Are You Happy cut for NIWRC, so it sets the series. It opens on the question card and her answer, then the sisterhood, then her message. All three answers are from one retake, because the crew asked her to redo the first take.
It is warm and community-centered. No harm on screen, no stock footage. B-roll is only the women at the reception.

Loops: L1 “Are you happy?” opens at 0:00 and closes at 0:11 (“for our communities”). L2 “What is her one message?” opens at 0:11 and closes on “safe and loved”. Stakes: women and children who deserve to be safe and loved.
do: Open on Christie with the hook text <q>Are you happy?</q> already on screen at 0:00.
Use the retake only: the answer from 00:31.6 and the message from 00:56.3.
Cut pauses over 0.7 s to about 0.25 s. Cut all crew talk.
Name super at 00:03, lower left, 2 s: Christie Modlin / Board Member, NIWRC.
Match Qendrim's approved NIWRC look: lower third, captions, color and pacing.
dont: Do not use the first take at 00:06 to 00:17 (“my family”). It was too quiet and the crew asked for a redo.
Do not use the message take 2 (the trafficking line). It is not in this clip.
Do not put “Iowa Tribe of Oklahoma” on screen. No Tribal affiliation on supers (NIWRC).
Do not use the tail “...missing or being abused”. This cut ends on “safe and loved”.
No logo, name or fade at 0:00.

decisions.b: The brief asked for “Secretary, Iowa Tribe of Oklahoma · NIWRC Board Member”. NIWRC says no Tribal affiliation on supers, so this plan uses “Board Member, NIWRC” (same as Shayna). Cory or Nick can confirm the title NIWRC wants.

The bites in the brief give about 21 s, not 30 to 45 s. Optional extra: “in a community where we don't have to feel like we're in danger” (01:09.4 end, about 5 s). The tail about “missing or being abused” stays out. Nick can say if he wants either added.

client_note: Why this matters: NIWRC wants Native women-led voices, shown with dignity and hope. This is the first Are You Happy cut for them. Her answer ties the series to the NIWRC mission.

[00:00.2] Alright, so we're always talking right to this camera, but Jo's going to ask you the questions. [do not use: crew talk]
[00:04.2] Alright, here we go. [do not use: crew talk]
[00:06.2] I'm happy. [do not use: first take, too quiet, crew asked for a redo]
[00:11.1] My source of happiness was my family. [do not use: first take, too quiet, crew asked for a redo]
[00:17.5] We'll have to speak up louder for this one. [do not use: crew talk]
[00:20.5] Ask happy again. [do not use: crew talk]
[00:22.5] Um, I'll just correct this. [do not use: crew talk]
[00:26.4] Okay. [do not use: crew talk]
[00:28.6] Ask from the top. [do not use: crew talk]
[00:30.6] From the top. [do not use: crew talk]
[00:31.6] I'm happy because I get to work with a great group of women here with NIWRC.
[00:41.3] And not only is the work we do, but the sisterhood that we have for our communities.
[00:56.3] That message would be that our women and children are precious.
[00:59.7] All of us are precious.
[01:01.7] And we deserve to be safe and loved in a community where we don't have to feel like we're in danger.
[01:09.7] In a community where we have fellowship and we don't have to worry about missing or being abused. [do not use: left out of this cut]
[01:19.6] Good job. That was it. [do not use: crew talk]
[01:20.0] (do not use anything after this point)
